newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to maintain limits on U.S. salmon boats.
newsitem.headline: Canada to maintain limits on U.S. salmon boats.

text.p: Locked in a feud over salmon fishing, Canada on Thursday rebuffed U.S. demands that it stop enforcing restrictions on American fishing vessels and in turn called on the United States to foster a better climate for potential negotiations.

"Canada will continue to enforce its regulations ...," Valerie Noftel, a spokeswoman for Canada's Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Ottawa, said. Instead, she suggested that "compliance by U.S. vessels would contribute to an improved atmosphere for the resumption of negotiations."

Sen. Frank Murkowski, a Republican from Alaska, sent a letter asking the U.S. Coast Guard to consider escorting American boats through Canadian waters. He said recent Canadian seizures of four U.S. boats "added injury to insult."
The two neighbours are at loggerheads over how to divide a dwindling salmon catch in the Pacific Northwest. After years of failed negotiations, the latest talks collapsed this month in Seattle.

Pressure for a deal was mounting before this year's salmon run begins in a few weeks. After a conversation between U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy last week, a new round of negotiations was scheduled for Friday.

But the United States on Tuesday decided to postpone the talks "until a more favourable climate for discussions can be achieved." It said Canada should drop its "threats" and stop seizing U.S. trawlers.

As a sign of its frustration, Canada last week began enforcing existing regulations against U.S. boats in its waters. Those require trawlers to alert Canadian authorities and stow their fishing gear when passing through the Canadian zone.

Canada in recent days has seized four U.S. boats that it accused of violating the rules. They were released after paying small fines, but the United States said the actions poisoned the atmosphere for discussions.

Albright and Axworthy talked briefly on Wednesday and agreed it was important to resume negotiations but neither made any commitments, Noftle said. She said the two were expected to speak again in the next few days.
